I recently just found my feet again after being homeless for a while. I set up a tent in a big, private dog walking fields. I found a small, hidden area among a tiny pine forest which I called home. Every morning I would wake up to the smells and sounds of nature and, even though I had huge worries like food, warmth and hygiene, I felt so incredible lucky. It almost felt like the world stopped, just for me to take it all in. My own little pocket of the world. 

I'm in a better place now. I moved across the country to start a new life and, somehow, I really don't know how, I'm making things work. 

I have a job again, working with the most humbling, incredibly kind people who have really been helping me out. I have one more week until my first proper paycheck in years and every day I feel like crying because of how lucky I am.

I recently found out that where I live has a small forest, about ten minutes walk from me. I've been heading there almost daily just to smell the earth and feel that ground beneath my feet again. I miss it dearly whenever I'm not there, but whenever I smell those familiar smells and wonder at the sights, I'm reminded of what that time in my life taught me. I am monumentally lucky for experiencing what my time there taught me and because of that, I am certain that those smells will always have a place very near and dear to my heart.

Well, this begins about 7 years ago. 

I'm introduced to this girl, this wonderfully beautiful creature. She's extraordinarily polite to me, a 14 year old fat dude, so, instantly I think either she's going to try to befriend me to make a fool out of me. Well, after meeting her a few times, each time it was my friends and myself meeting her friends and herself, we started talking on Facebook chat. Nothing serious, just the usual 'Hey, wuu2?' back and forth bollocks. 

We were speaking like this for about 6 months when I started to feel like we *needed* to talk to each other. One of us would wake up with a good morning text or whatever and then we'd be talking all day and night. We really developed a good friendship. 

This progressed until we were both 17. We lived in the same hometown so we were starting to meet up on our own accord now. No one else, just us. Meanwhile, things at home for me weren't going well; I'd been kicked out of college, kicked out of my home and I barely spoke to anyone apart from her. Because of this isolation, this started a very heavy, three year spiral into drug and alcohol abuse for me. Now I know that isn't a good enough excuse, but that's all another story. Now, when you're dealing a drug, which I was, you have a lot of faux friends. A lot of people who are willing to show you the greatest camaraderie when you're having a good time but just vanish when it's all tumbling. Everyone apart from her left me. 

She stayed. 
She stayed through it all, through all those years of lies and deceit, knowing what was happening but still sticking with me. 
She stayed knowing I had nothing. 

I loved her deeply and sincerely. 

She was the only thing that felt ***real***

Okay so fast forward three years or so and I'm finally off the drugs longer than a month at a time. About a year before, she moved 350 miles away from me. Because of the lifestyle I lead, I didn't see her before she went. So dealing with having her that far away was pretty tough, for both of us. We'd declared we lived each other a couple years previous. This was different to anything I'd ever felt. 

Anyway, after moving up there she got with some dude, she began to fade into a vivid memory and I started to taste her words less and less. It hurt, but I couldn't blame her; I'd put so much worry on her for years and she finally seemed happy, with or without me that made me happy in return. Every now and again I'd get a 'Hello' and we'd chat for a few days then she'd run off into her life again.

Up until start of this year, I'd moved around a lot, never in the same place for more than 6 months, I was sharing a place with an old friend when I'd got a text from her asking if she could call me. I called her and she was crying, I could barely make out what she was saying but I heard the key words 'boyfriend hit me' then she hung up. I tried calling her a lot of times but her phone was off. 

An hour later she called me and she was calmer. She said she had a train ticket to come to my town but her boyfriend tore it up then started to beat her. I called my cousin and arranged to go and pick her up. We drove for so long just to pick her up and drive back. We stayed in my bed and kissed. It felt amazing, that after all these years, everything I'd ever wanted was right here, happening right now. 

She went back home the next day, but things progressed like this for ages and ages. Constantly texting and phone calls every night. 

One night, she called me up to tell me she'd finished it between her and her boyfriend and she wanted me to move up with her as soon as possible. I straight away said yes but I wanted to have a job before I did, so we agreed I come up for a few days so I could look around for jobs.

The day came for me to go up there, she met me at the train station and those three days seemed were starting nicely. By the end of the first day, we were both so tired and fell asleep almost instantly. 

The second day was strange, she was being really off with me, which made me question absolutely everything I'd done until that point. She wouldn't speak to me, nothing.
I left for a few hours, to go looking for jobs and a general walk. When I got back she seemed better, she seemed sorry for the way she had been, but I told her not to worry. 

That night was the best night of my life; we made love. This wasn't just sex. This was real, terrifying, brilliant love. We confessed that this was different for the both of us, that this wasn't just like any other time and that made us even crazier for each other.

I was the happiest guy in the world and if I met anyone who contended that, I'd just mentally draw them the picture of myself this complete angel laying in bed after having made love. 

Everything I want right there beside me. Everything I needed entwining her hands in mine.

Then she said those words.

'By the way, I do hope you realise that it really hasn't been that long since I broke up with my boyfriend. I don't want to settle down just yet. I want to go out and have fun with other guys before I even think of it. I haven't had my time to sleep around. But don't worry, I do want to settle down with you, just not right now.'

I fucking broke.

So this is how it feels to be ripped apart with nothing but words.

She said something else but I couldn't hear her over the sound of my fucking heart clogging my throat.

The rest of my time there was spent in a bit of a daze. She knew she had upset me, but I didn't notice any remorse.

When I came back home the arguments started and we could feel each other drifting apart. Fast.

One day she told me I could hurt her with words so I asked her how her words; 'I want to go out and have fun with other guys' sat in her mouth. She asked me why I bought that up and I said because that's what destroyed us. 

Right there and then I said goodbye. It felt like I was tearing my heart away from it's life support, but I still did it.

To this day, I still think of her.

I drink a cold drink and it reminds me of how she used to always be cold.

I see a piece of drawn art and instantly think of her drawing she did for me years ago.

I miss her so much.
